text:
kevin: Trying an experiment — combine a short probe window + surge tokens for spot-backed inference fleets. Goal: reduce cold-scale cost while avoiding big eviction spikes. Thoughts?

anya: I like it. Can you sketch how probe window works end-to-end? e.g., do we spin small warm nodes first, route a tiny % of traffic, then if healthy expand? :thinking_face:

kevin: Exactly. Flow I mocked: 1) trigger scale decision -> allocate `warm_probe_size` preemptible GPUs in a probe zone (different AZ) 2) run traffic at 1-5% for `probe_window` seconds 3) if p50/p95 latencies within SLO and no OOMs -> consume `surge_tokens` to scale full pool; else backoff and try other pools.

maria: Concern: eviction bursts can still kill probes mid-window and create flip-flop. How do we treat probe failures vs real failures?

kevin: Good point. Proposal: treat probe failures as "soft-fail" unless we see >=2 probe instances fail within the window. Soft-fail -> try next candidate pool (mixed GPU types) + autofall back to smaller model variant. Hard-fail -> halt scale and drop surge token.

liam: Config suggestion (yaml prototype):

```
autoscale:
  scale_up_threshold: 0.70    # queue depth / util
  warm_probe_size: 2         # GPUs to spin for probe
  probe_window: 25s          # sample duration
  probe_traffic_pct: 3%      # percent of incoming requests
  surge_tokens: 1            # number of simultaneous burst grants
  cooldown: 150s             # full scale cooldown
  soft_fail_backoff: 45s
  max_multi_pool_attempts: 2
```

anya: +1 to limiting probe_traffic_pct. Keep it tiny to avoid cost and noisy metrics. Also put a histogram-based p95 check, not just avg.

maria: We should also aggressively log probe metadata to traces: pool_id, instance_lifetime, preempted=true/false, loss_fraction. That helps model eviction probability for that pool.

ops-bot: deploy notice: autoscaler/probe-window feature flag toggled ON for canary orgs at 1709501300. Monitor `autoscaler.probe.success_rate` and `fleet.eviction.rate` dashboards.

kevin: For safety, add a surge token bank per-region that decays over time instead of instant replenish. E.g. bank size = 2, regen_rate = 1 per 10m. Helps limit cross-region bursts and cost surprises.

liam: Also consider a CPU-render fallback lane: when probe fails AND global spot scarcity high, route low-priority traffic to CPU-only or quantized smaller model. Keeps latency predictable for critical routes.

maria: What about billing signals? We need per-request tokenized cost estimate so owners see impact of using surge tokens. Maybe add `surge_cost_estimate` to the rollout UI.

kevin: Yep — rough numbers from canary: probe window cost ~= 0.12$/probe for 2xA10 25s. If surge avoids a 30s cold-start for 100 QPS, saves ~1.5$ in GPU time. So win in many cases but needs visibility.

anya: Implementation notes: - prefer AZ-hedged probes when possible - if using multi-cloud, prefer probe in lower-interruption region first - adopt exponential backoff when repeated soft-fails per pool

liam: Metric triggers we bumped in the test cluster: scale_up when pending_queue_util > 0.7 for 3s OR sustained token bucket deficit; scale_down cooldown increased to 5m to avoid churn.

maria: Danger: network egress spikes when spinning new nodes for model weights. Ensure we prefetch weights into warm_probe image (init container).

kevin: Good call — add `prefetch: true` to probe pod spec; if prefetch fails, mark probe soft-fail early.

anya: Observability checklist before broader rollout: probe success rate, median probe start-to-ready, probe preempt rate, cost per successful scale, fraction of scales that used multi-pool fallback, p95 latency delta post-scale.

liam: For canary run: roll to 10% of inference traffic for three hours, then evaluate. ops-bot, pls keep alerting verbose for first 6 hours.

ops-bot: noted. Alerts: `high_probe_preempt_rate`, `surge_token_exhaustion`, `scale_flap_detected`.

kevin: Thanks all — I'll push RFC draft with the yaml above and a short experiment plan. Will ping when RFC ready. :thumbsup:

anya: :eyes:

maria: Thanks — excited to see results.
